source_text:
ὁ δὲ
θεὸς τῆς εἰρήνης ποιήσει μεθ' ἡμῶν κατὰ τὴν αὑτοῦ φιλανθρωπίαν εἰς τὸ
συντριβῆναι τὸν σατανᾶν ὑπὸ τοὺς πόδας ἡμῶν τῶν Χριστιανῶν καὶ ἀποδιωχθῆναι
πᾶσαν πρόφασιν πονηρὰν εἰς τὸ μὴ σχισθῆναι τὸν σύνδεσμον ἐξ ἡμῶν τῆς τοῦ
Χριστοῦ ἀνυποκρίτου ἀγάπης καὶ εἰρήνης καὶ ὀρθῆς πίστεως καὶ ἀληθείας.
thought_title: Prayer for peace and unbroken bond
orientation: Epiphanius, having just quoted Scripture against grumbling, now prays that God will crush Satan and preserve the bond of love, peace, faith, and truth among Christians.
pass_a_gloss: But the God of peace will do with us according to his love for humankind, so that Satan is crushed under the feet of us Christians and every wicked pretext is driven away, so that the bond is not torn from us of Christ's unfeigned love and peace and right faith and truth.

choices.why: The δέ marks a contrast with the preceding warning against grumbling; 'God of peace' is a fixed Pauline phrase kept literal.

choices.english: according to his love for humankind
choices.why: φιλανθρωπία is a key patristic term for God's benevolent disposition toward humans; rendered as a noun phrase rather than an adjective to preserve its weight.

choices.term: εἰς τὸ συντριβῆναι τὸν σατανᾶν ὑπὸ τοὺς πόδας ἡμῶν
choices.english: so that Satan is crushed under the feet of us
choices.why: The εἰς τό + infinitive construction expresses purpose; the passive infinitive keeps Satan as the one acted upon, matching the source's syntax.
rejected: to crush Satan under our feet
for the crushing of Satan under our feet

choices.english: every wicked pretext is driven away
choices.why: ἀποδιώκω means to chase away or drive off; 'pretext' captures πρόφασις as a specious excuse or occasion for evil.

choices.term: εἰς τὸ μὴ σχισθῆναι τὸν σύνδεσμον ἐξ ἡμῶν
choices.english: so that the bond is not torn from us
choices.why: σχίζω means to split or tear apart; the passive with ἐξ ἡμῶν indicates the bond being torn away from the community, preserving the source's spatial metaphor.
rejected: so that the bond may not be broken among us
lest the bond be severed from us

choices.why: ἀνυπόκριτος means without hypocrisy or pretense; 'unfeigned' is the traditional English rendering and keeps the negative prefix visible.

bible_refs.note: The phrase 'God of peace' and the crushing of Satan under feet echo Romans 16:20, though the wording here is adapted.

pass_b_english: But the God of peace, in his love for humankind, will act with us so that Satan is crushed under the feet of us Christians, and every wicked pretext is driven away, so that the bond of Christ's unfeigned love, peace, right faith, and truth is not torn from us.
